en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Cittalatā Grove, from the Section on Female Vimānas.
5. The Mansion of Bhadditthi “Blue and yellow, black,
as well as madder-red and crimson;”
Surrounded by the filaments of various kinds of flowers,
including mandārava blossoms.
You wear a garland upon your head;
O wise one, there are no such trees in other bodies.
By what means were you born in this glorious body among the Tāvatiṃsa gods?
O goddess, being asked, please explain.
“What is the fruit of this karma?
“They knew me as Bhadditthikā,
a female lay follower in Kimilā.”
Endowed with faith and virtue,
always delighting in sharing,
[giving] clothing and food—
Having lit lamps for the dwellings,
I gave them to those who have become upright,
with a mind full of serene confidence.
On the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles—
Endowed with the eight factors,
I shall observe the Uposatha,
always restrained in my virtuous conduct.
Through restraint and sharing,
we dwell in a celestial mansion;
we abstain from taking life.
Restrained from false speech,
and far removed from theft, sexual misconduct,
and the drinking of intoxicants.
Delighting in the five precepts and skilled in the Noble Truths,
these lay disciples belong to the One with Vision.
Dwelling in heedfulness,
having completed my residence and accomplished what was wholesome, I have passed away from there and now roam through Nandana, self-luminous.
I fed the bhikkhus who were supremely compassionate for my welfare,
as well as the pair of ascetics and the Great Sage;
having completed their dwellings and performed wholesome deeds, they passed away from there.
Self-luminous, I wandered through the Nandana grove.
I constantly observed the eightfold Uposatha, which brings immeasurable happiness.
“Having completed my dwelling and accomplished what is wholesome, passing away from there,
I now roam at will in the Nandana Grove, self-luminous.
The Fifth Vimāna of Bhadditthī.
